title: Analysis of reactive astrogliosis in mouse brain using in situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry
author: Muraleedharan, Nardini, et al.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse and prepare for perfusion
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in an isoflurane chamber, then inject a ketamine/xylazine mixture (up to 80 mg kg⁻¹ ketamine and 10 mg kg⁻¹ xylazine dissolved in saline) intraperitoneally using a 27‑gauge needle and 1 mL syringe; confirm deep anesthesia with a toe‑pinch response before proceeding.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize mouse in isoflurane chamber.
Prepare ketamine/xylazine solution (≤80 mg kg⁻¹ ketamine, 10 mg kg⁻¹ xylazine).
Inject intraperitoneally with 27‑gauge needle, 1 mL syringe.
Verify lack of toe‑pinch response.

steps.title: Cardiac perfusion with saline then PFA
steps.instruction: Secure the anesthetized mouse on its back, make a 5–6 cm lateral incision, open the diaphragm, insert a 30‑gauge needle into the posterior left ventricle, cut the right atrium to create an outlet, attach the outlet port, set the perfusion pressure to 80 mm Hg, perfuse with saline for 10 min, then switch to 4 % (w/v) PFA in PBS (prepared at 55 °C, filtered) and perfuse for 10–15 min.

substeps.instruction: Place mouse supine on shallow tray.
Make 5–6 cm lateral incision and open diaphragm.
Insert 30‑gauge needle into posterior left ventricle lumen.
Incise right atrium with iris scissors to create outlet.
Attach outlet port and set manometer to 80 mm Hg.
Perfuse saline for 10 min.
Switch stopcock to 4 % PFA/PBS (same flow rate).
Perfuse PFA for 10–15 min.

steps.title: Dissect brain and post‑fix tissue
steps.instruction: Cut posterior to the ears to separate the head, remove skin from the skull, cut along the midline to detach parietal and frontal bone plates, lift the brain out, place it in ≥10 × its volume of fixative (4 % PFA/PBS), swirl occasionally, and fix 3 × 3 mm biopsies in freshly prepared 4 % PFA/PBS for 12–18 h (wear PPE and handle PFA in a safety cabinet).

substeps.instruction: Separate head with scissors posterior to ears.
Make caudal midline skin incision and remove skin rostrally.
Cut skull along midline and between eyes; snap off bone plates with tweezers.
Tilt brain upward, cut optic and cranial nerves, lift brain out.
Transfer brain to vial containing ≥10 × brain volume of 4 % PFA/PBS; swirl occasionally.
Fix 3 × 3 mm biopsies in fresh 4 % PFA/PBS for 12–18 h.

steps.title: Cryoprotect brain in sucrose solutions
steps.instruction: After fixation, incubate the whole brain in 15 % sucrose for 2–3 h, then transfer to 30 % sucrose for 12–18 h before embedding.

substeps.instruction: Place brain in 15 % sucrose; incubate 2–3 h.
Transfer brain to 30 % sucrose; incubate 12–18 h.

steps.title: Embed brain in freezing compound and freeze
steps.instruction: Label plastic molds with orientation marks (protect with clear tape), cover the bottom with NEG50 or OCT freezing compound, pre‑chill acetone in a petri dish on dry‑ice pellets to create a slurry, remove brain from 30 % sucrose, blot excess liquid, place brain upright in the mold, gently mix with NEG50, orient as desired, cover with NEG50, then freeze quickly by placing the mold on the acetone/dry‑ice slurry until the block becomes fully white and solid; dry the mold bottom, wrap with aluminum foil or parafilm, label, and store.

substeps.instruction: Label plastic molds with permanent marker; protect label with clear tape.
Cover mold bottom with NEG50 or OCT.
Pre‑chill acetone in a petri dish on dry‑ice pellets; add enough acetone to cover the bottom and create a bubbling slurry.
Remove brain from 30 % sucrose, blot excess liquid on a Kimwipe, place on ice dish, trim bottom if needed.
Place brain into mold, gently mix with NEG50, orient for optimal sectioning.
Cover tissue with NEG50 and fill mold.
Freeze by placing mold on acetone/dry‑ice slurry; ensure acetone reaches only the bottom quarter of the mold.
Allow block to become fully white and solid; dry mold bottom with paper towel.
Wrap block with aluminum foil or parafilm, label, and store.

steps.title: Store frozen blocks
steps.instruction: Keep the frozen blocks at –20 °C for short‑term storage (≤5 days) or at –80 °C for long‑term storage; never allow thawing, and transport on dry ice.

steps.title: Count GFAP‑positive cells in ImageJ
steps.instruction: Using ImageJ, draw equal‑area boxes over each region, employ the Cell Counter plugin to count GFAP‑positive cells on every 12th section; for cortical layers count all cells within a 250‑µm‑wide column from white matter to pial surface, exclude cells with unclear morphology, analyze at least five sections per group, and apply the same method to combined GFAP/Lcn2 or GFAP/C3 stained sections.

substeps.instruction: Open ImageJ and load stained section image.
Draw boxes of identical area over each region of interest.
Use the Cell Counter plugin to count GFAP‑positive cells.
Count cells on every 12th section.
For cortical layers, count cells in a 250‑µm‑wide column from white matter to pial surface.
Exclude cells whose morphology is not clearly visible.
Analyze at least 5 sections per experimental group.
Apply identical counting procedure to GFAP/Lcn2 or GFAP/C3 combined ISH/IHC sections.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the cell‑count data with Prism software (version 4) using one‑way ANOVA; consider results statistically significant when p ≤ 0.05.

substeps.instruction: Import data into Prism v4.
Run one‑way ANOVA.
Record p‑values; significance defined as p ≤ 0.05.
